title: 8. 记忆对于历史的效用与弊害
originalTitle: 8. On the Utility and Liability of Memory for History

children: 8. On the Utility and Liability of Memory for History

zh: 8. 记忆对于历史的效用与弊害

en: The thesis gathered from our analysis of the déjà vu told us that the ‘end of history’ is a state of mind that takes root precisely where the very historicity of experience has come into relief, precisely where even the genesis of historical time is in question. The apparent collapse

(carefully conceals yet also unwillingly signals) a real tuning fork. This thesis exclusively regards concepts that concern the functioning of memory: the memory of the present, anachronism, etc. Up to this point, however, it has been used to interpret and criticise Kojève’s representation of the ‘end of history’, which does not in fact mention the role of memory, but rather interpellates phenomena of quite a different kind. Namely, the decline of Labour and Politics, the animalistic nature of the American way of life, and Japanese snobbery. We now need, then, to take a further step.
zh: 我们从既视现象的分析中得出的命题告诉我们：“历史终结”是一种心境，它恰恰扎根于经验的历史性本身凸显之处，扎根于历史时间的生成也成为问题之处。表面上的崩溃揭示出一个真实的音叉——它小心遮掩这个音叉，却又不情愿地发出信号。这个命题只涉及同记忆运作有关的概念：对当下的记忆、时代错置，等等。然而到目前为止，我们一直用它解释和批评科耶夫关于“历史终结”的表述；科耶夫实际上并未提及记忆的作用，而是援引了性质完全不同的现象，即劳动与政治的衰退、美国生活方式的动物性和日本式势利主义。因此，我们现在必须再向前走一步。

en: This thesis should be confronted with a text that

imputes the breakdown of historical praxis to the mnestic faculty. We must say immediately that such a comparison demands a partial change of perspective. The thesis here takes on a self-reflective tenor: the functioning of memory appears simultaneously as the
and the
, a deep-seated model and a phenomenon at surface-level, a central thread and a maze, the pivot of the solution and the cause of the problem. Here, our task is no longer to outline analogies or spot

similarities between the existential experience of memory and the contemporary public mood, but rather to understand how (and with what consequences) this experience has itself acquired immediate public importance. Rather than limit ourselves to deciphering certain forms of life by bringing in the outside aid of mnestic processes, it is necessary also to interrogate the forms of life that these processes themselves foment.
zh: 这个命题应当同一篇把历史实践的崩坏直接归因于记忆官能的文本相对照。必须立即说明，这种比较要求我们部分改变视角。此时，命题带上了一种自我反思色彩：记忆的运作同时显现为解释项（explicans）与被解释项（explicandum），既是深层模式又是表层现象，既是中心线索又是迷宫，既是解决问题的枢轴又是问题的成因。我们的任务不再是在记忆的生存经验与当代公共心境之间勾勒类比或发现相似，而是理解这种经验自身如何、以及以何种后果，取得了直接的公共意义。我们不能只借助外来的记忆过程来解读某些生活形式；还必须追问这些过程本身所促成的生活形式。

en: In the second of his

, entitled ‘On the utility and liability of history for life’, Nietzsche maintains that an over-abundance of memory paralyses action, cuts off the future, and encourages melancholy: ‘Imagine the most extreme example, a human being who does not possess the power to forget, who is damned to see becoming everywhere; such a human being … would hardly even dare to lift a finger. All action requires forgetting, just as the existence of all organic things requires not only light, but darkness as well.’

The mounting mass of memories implies an enormous growth in historical consciousness and historiographical knowledge. But untrammelled dedication to the past, instilling the belief that we are its late-flowering fruits and its epigones, ultimately undermines history itself: ‘at the point of a certain excess of history, life crumbles and degenerates – as does, ultimately, as a result of this degeneration, history itself, as well’.
zh: 尼采在《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇《历史对于生命的效用与弊害》中主张，记忆过度充盈会使行动瘫痪，切断未来，并助长忧郁：“试想一个最极端的例子：一个没有遗忘能力、注定要处处看见生成的人；这样一个人……恐怕连一根手指也不敢抬起。一切行动都需要遗忘，正如一切有机物的存在不仅需要光，也同样需要黑暗。”
不断堆积的记忆意味着历史意识和史学知识大幅增长。但是，对过去不受约束的投入使人相信自己是过去晚熟的果实和后来者，最终却会破坏历史本身：“历史一旦过度到某一点，生命便会崩坏和退化；而这种退化最终也会使历史本身同样崩坏。”

en: History gets worn out and stumbles precisely
memory becomes hypertrophic. While ‘historical human beings’ are able to ‘utilize the past for life’,
placing it at

the service of an action that looks to the future, ‘passive’ and ‘backward-looking’ individuals of modern times allow themselves to be hypnotised by memories, cultivating them as a good in themselves, no longer being able to select among them in view of some new endeavour. Or so Nietzsche says. Now, however, we must ask ourselves: in what kind of predicament does memory achieve a troubling autonomy from the tasks of life, expanding beyond measure? In one case, above all: when it takes the present as its own object, treating it as something that has already been – that is, when we have the feeling of déjà vu. According to Bergson, if in general ‘consciousness, attentive to life, only admits, legally, those [memories] which can offer their guidance to action’,

in the event of déjà vu we mainly remember the superfluous, namely the very thing that we are perceiving in the current moment: ‘what can be more unavailing of our present action than the memory of the present?’

Unavailing, but also harmful. Employing expressions almost identical to those that Nietzsche uses to point to the difficulties caused by an exorbitant feeling for history, Bergson correlates the mnestic pathology to ‘a weakening or impairing of our attention to outward life’, the ‘feeling that the future is closed’, a ‘state of apathy and inertia’.
zh: 历史恰恰因为记忆过度肥大而磨损、踉跄。“历史的人”能够“为生命利用过去”

，让过去服务于面向未来的行动；现代“被动”而“向后看”的个人则任由记忆催眠，把记忆本身视为值得追求的事物而悉心培植，再也无法着眼于某项新事业而从中作出选择——至少尼采是这样说的。然而，我们现在必须追问：在何种困境中，记忆才会脱离生命任务而取得一种令人不安的自主性，并无限膨胀？首要情形只有一个：当记忆把当下当作自己的对象，把它作为已经发生之物处理，也就是当我们产生既视感时。依照柏格森的说法，一般而言，“专注于生命的意识，按其法则只容许那些能够为行动提供指导的［记忆］进入”；
既视感出现时，我们记住的却主要是多余之物，也就是我们此刻正在知觉的东西：“还有什么比对当下的记忆对我们当前行动更加无用？”
它不仅无用，而且有害。柏格森使用了几乎同尼采用来指明过度历史感所致困难完全相同的表述，把记忆病理同“我们对外部生活之注意的减弱或受损”、“未来已经封闭的感觉”以及“冷漠和惰性的状态”联系起来。

en: The hypertrophy of memory, from which the consumption and blockage of history derive, is made up of déjà vu. People for whom the present seems wholly dependent on the past, like an echo of the original sound, are no longer historical (they are now incapable, that is, of carrying out
genuinely historical actions). But no

past is of such considerable authority as to impose such a dependency. No sequence of events that has really happened deserves to be emblazoned with the title of an untouchable, binding archetype. Rather, the past that subjects those afflicted by hypermnesia to itself is a
-past. Only a fictitious ‘once upon a time’ could demand that it be reproduced in every detail by the current

. To put it better: in the experience of déjà vu, it is only the fantastical ‘once upon a time’ that holds stage. Those who are sheepishly obsequious to what has been, are in effect obsequious to ‘now’ itself, projected back in time. And in so far as we have a memory of this ‘now’ already as we experience it, it constitutes an illusory and yet overbearing ‘back then’ (indeed, it is overbearing because it is illusory), faced with which we must inevitably behave mimetically. In the epoch in which the
present seems to have to retrace the
present, with the scruple of the epigone and the destructive melancholy of the late-flowering fruit, people indulge in a resignation-streaked fatalism.
zh: 造成历史耗损和堵塞的记忆肥大，是由既视感构成的。对于那些觉得当下完全依赖过去、仿佛只是原声之回响的人来说，他们已经不再具有历史性；也就是说，他们已经无法实行真正的历史行动。然而，没有任何真实过去拥有如此巨大的权威，足以强加这种依赖。没有任何确实发生过的事件序列，配得上不可触碰、具有约束力的原型这一显赫称号。相反，使记忆亢进者屈从于它的那个过去，是一个伪过去。只有虚构的“从前”才会要求当前的此时此地在每一个细节上将其复制。说得更准确些：在既视感经验中，占据舞台的只有幻想的“从前”。那些怯懦地谄媚既往之物的人，实际上是在谄媚被向后投进时间的“现在”本身。只要我们在经历这个“现在”时已经拥有对它的记忆，它就会构成一个虚幻却专横的“那时”——它恰恰因为虚幻才如此专横——面对它，我们不可避免地只能模仿。在被知觉的当下仿佛必须以后来者的谨慎和晚熟果实的毁灭性忧郁，重新描摹被记住的当下的时代，人们沉溺于一种夹带屈从的宿命论。

en: The déjà vu phenomenon establishes a bridge between the second of the

and what Nietzsche called the ‘thought of thoughts’: the eternal return of the identical type. The weakening of life’s (and history’s) potential, attributed in his 1874 text to a vertiginous increase in memory-activity, is expressed most vividly in the refrain with which he subsequently proclaimed nihilism (in a passage of
): ‘All is empty, all is alike, all hath been!’
If all has been, every

event today repeats a previous event and is in turn destined to be infinitely repeated. A chilling perspective: we cannot do anything but grit our teeth at the thought of a life where ‘there will be nothing new in it’.
Far from alleviating the weight of nihilism, the idea of an eternal return brings it to fever pitch. It gives a cosmological value (‘time itself is a circle’)

to the typical illusion of déjà vu. But such a formulation of the doctrine is too-readily awestruck: in a sense it is gloomy and nightmarish, yet it is also superficial, an ‘organ grinder’s song’ making things simple for itself.
zh: 既视现象在《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇与尼采所谓“思想中的思想”——相同者的永恒回归（eternal return of the identical）——之间架起了一座桥。1874年的文章把生命（以及历史）潜能的削弱归因于记忆活动令人眩晕的增长；后来，尼采宣告虚无主义时的一句反复吟唱（见《查拉图斯特拉如是说》）最鲜明地表达了这种削弱：“一切皆空，一切相同，一切都已经发生！”
如果一切都已经发生，那么今天的每个事件都在重复先前事件，并且自身也注定会被无限重复。这是一幅令人胆寒的图景：想到一种“其中不会有任何新事物”的生活，我们除了咬紧牙关，什么也做不了。
永恒回归观念非但没有减轻虚无主义的重量，反而使之达到沸点；它把一种宇宙论价值——“时间本身就是一个圆环”
——赋予既视感的典型幻觉。不过，这种教义表述太轻易地拜倒在自身造成的震惊面前：它一方面阴郁而梦魇般可怖，另一方面又流于肤浅，不过是一首替自己省事的“街头手摇琴之歌”。

en: The thought of an eternal return is counterposed to nihilism, first and foremost to the nihilist version of the eternal return (already presaged in some pages of the second of the

). The pernicious spell that compels us to consider an action in the making as the duplication of some prior action is thwarted if only we ask ourselves what the model-action really is. We have just observed how, when we fall mercy to déjà vu, we seem to be repeating something, but we cannot say
that we are repeating: the specific content of the repetition is established only by the actual experience,

and it is up to the ‘now’ to determine the ‘already-been’ retroactively. And yet, as soon as it usurps the paradoxical structure of déjà vu, rather than indulging the illusory and paralysing effects that it produces, the doctrine of the eternal return serves as an antidote to nihilism. If the gesture that I now perform necessarily had to conform even in the slightest detail to some particular gesture performed in the past, it would not even be worth lifting a finger. But this is not the case. According to Nietzsche, only the present moment can decide what has already been; the action now underway has the task of establishing the
that it is called upon to reiterate; it is the

’s prerogative to create the event that it is bringing back. Heidegger recapitulated this decisive aspect of Nietzsche’s ‘thought of thoughts’ with words that could fully figure in any sober account of the déjà vu:
zh: 永恒回归思想首先反对虚无主义，尤其反对永恒回归的虚无主义版本——这个版本已经在《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇的若干段落中露出端倪。只要我们追问那项范型行动实际上是什么，那个迫使我们把正在形成的行动看成某项先前行动之复制的有害魔咒，就会遭到挫败。我们刚刚看到：当既视感支配我们时，我们仿佛正在重复某个东西，却说不清重复的究竟是什么；重复的具体内容只有通过现实经验才能确定，必须由“现在”追溯性地决定“已经发生”。然而，一旦永恒回归教义接过既视感的悖论结构，而不是纵容它所产生的幻觉性、瘫痪性效果，它便成为虚无主义的解毒剂。如果我此刻作出的动作必然要在最细微之处也符合过去某项特定动作，那么连抬起一根手指都不值得。但事情并非如此。尼采认为，只有当前时刻能够决定什么已经发生；正在展开的行动负有确定那个它被要求重复的“什么”（quid）的任务；创造它正在带回的事件，是此时此地的特权。海德格尔用一段完全可以收入任何冷静的既视现象说明中的话，概括了尼采“思想中的思想”的这一决定性面向：

en: Whatever is or is to be will be decided in and by Dasein, inasmuch as only those aspects of Becoming that were once a part of my life are destined to come again. But then do we know what once was? No! Can we ever know such things? We know nothing of an earlier life. Everything we are now living we experience for the first time, although now and again in the midst of our ordinary experiences that strange and obscure experience crops up which says: What you are now experiencing, precisely in the form it is now taking, you have experienced once before … what will come again when it recurs? The answer to that question is: whatever will be in the next moment.
zh: 存在之物或将要存在之物，将在此在（Dasein）之中并由此在作出决定，因为只有那些曾经属于我生命的生成面向，才注定会再次到来。那么，我们知道曾经存在的是什么吗？不知道！我们能够知道这种事情吗？我们对先前的生命一无所知。我们此刻生活的一切都是第一次经验，尽管在日常经验之中，偶尔会浮现一种奇异而晦暗的经验，向我们说道：你此刻正在经验的东西——恰恰以它此刻采取的形式——你从前已经经验过一次……那么，当它再次回返时，将要到来的是什么？这个问题的答案是：下一时刻将会存在的一切。

en: Let us pick up the main thread of our discourse again. History stops because memory becomes hypertrophic; the hypertrophy of memory, which prevents history from acting, consists of déjà vu. The questions raised by the second of the

(excess of memory, excess of history) were expounded again in close connection with the contemporary situation. One question in particular seems unavoidable: how has the déjà vu attained the rank of a collective phenomenon, such that the customs and mentality of the so-called ‘post-modern’ epoch bear its imprint? Why has it been transformed from a private, exceptional episode into such a manifest, widespread circumstance? Or, if you prefer: for what reason has the déjà vu taken on a

significance, and, indeed, how come we can point to the déjà vu as the historical fact in which the idea of an ‘end of history’ is rooted (and which validates this idea)? In answering this, we need once again to pay the greatest attention to what we grasped at the very outset: the coexistence within the déjà vu of two aspects that are not only distinct, but moreover contradictory.
zh: 现在，让我们重新拾起论述的主线。历史之所以停顿，是因为记忆变得过度肥大；阻止历史行动的记忆肥大，由既视感构成。《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇提出的问题（记忆过剩、历史过剩），已经在同当代处境的紧密联系中得到重新阐述。有一个问题尤其无法回避：既视感是如何上升为集体现象，以至所谓“后现代”时代的习俗和心态都带上了它的印记？它为何会从私人而异常的插曲，转化为如此明显而普遍的情形？或者换一种问法：既视感出于什么原因取得了历史意义？我们为何能够把既视现象指认为“历史终结”观念赖以扎根并获得证实的历史事实？要回答这个问题，我们必须再次高度关注一开始就把握到的东西：既视现象内部两个不仅有别、而且彼此矛盾的面向同时存在。
Keith Ansell Pearson and Duncan Large, eds., The Nietzsche Reader, Oxford: Blackwell, 2006, p. 127。

zh: Nietzsche, Gay Science, New York: Dover Publications, 2006, §341。“假如有一天或一夜，一个恶魔潜入你最孤独的孤独，对你说：‘你此刻正在生活、并且一直生活着的这个生命，你还必须再活一次，并且还要活无数次；其中不会有任何新事物，你生命中的每一种痛苦、每一种欢乐、每一个思想、每一声叹息，以及一切难以言说的渺小与伟大，都必须再次来到你面前，而且次序和顺序全然相同——这只蜘蛛、林间这片月光也一样，这个时刻和我本人也一样。存在的永恒沙漏将不断再次翻转，而你也将随之一同翻转，你这粒尘埃！’——你难道不会扑倒在地，咬牙切齿，诅咒说出这番话的恶魔吗？”
en: Nietzsche,

, New York: Dover Publications 2006, §341. ‘What if a demon crept after thee into thy loneliest loneliness some day or night, and said to thee: “This life, as thou livest it at present, and hast lived it, thou must live it once more, and also innumerable times; and there will be nothing new in it, but every pain and every joy and every thought and every sigh, and all the unspeakably small and great in thy life must come to thee again, and all in the same series and sequence – and similarly this spider and this moonlight among the trees, and similarly this moment, and I myself. The eternal sand-glass of existence will ever be turned once more, and thou with it, thou speck of dust!” – Wouldst thou not throw thyself down and gnash thy teeth, and curse the demon that so spake?’
